meera.name: Dr. Meera Iyer

kavya.name: Kavya Menon
kavya.bio: Kavya has performed more than 10,000 laser sessions and set up laser safety programs for multi-city clinic chains. She specialises in laser hair reduction for darker skin types and in practical, hands-on training.

arjun.name: Dr. Arjun Rao
arjun.bio: Arjun is a cosmetologist focused on chemical peels and acne management. He runs a busy skin clinic in Hyderabad and teaches practitioners how to get great results while keeping complications rare.

courses.title: Certified Laser Hair Reduction Technician
courses.short: Become a job-ready laser hair reduction technician with clinic-grade protocols for Indian skin types.
courses.long: This 8-week accelerator takes you from laser physics fundamentals to confidently running laser hair reduction sessions in a clinic. You will learn how different wavelengths interact with hair and skin, how to assess clients across the Fitzpatrick types common in India, how to select safe parameters on diode, Nd:YAG and alexandrite systems, and how to manage aftercare and side effects. Every module ends with an assessment so you can prove competence before moving on.
outcomes: Explain selective photothermolysis and how wavelength, fluence and pulse duration affect results
Assess clients using Fitzpatrick skin typing adapted for Indian skin
Run a structured consultation and identify contraindications
Select safe starting parameters on diode, Nd:YAG and alexandrite lasers
Deliver clear aftercare advice and manage common side effects

certification.title: Laser Hair Reduction Technician Certificate
certification.description: Pass all three module assessments to earn a certificate you can show to clinics and employers.

outcomeHighlights.title: Clinic Ready
outcomeHighlights.description: Graduates are prepared to join dermatology and laser clinics as technicians.

outcomeHighlights.title: High-Demand Skill
outcomeHighlights.description: Laser hair reduction is one of the fastest-growing aesthetic services in India.

outcomeHighlights.title: Safety First
outcomeHighlights.description: Protocols designed specifically for Fitzpatrick types III–V.

lessons.title: How Lasers Interact with Skin and Hair
lessons.summary: Laser hair reduction works by selective photothermolysis: light energy is absorbed by melanin in the hair follicle and converted to heat, damaging the follicle while sparing the surrounding skin.
points: Wavelength decides which chromophore absorbs the energy: melanin, haemoglobin or water.
Pulse duration should match the thermal relaxation time of the follicle so heat stays where it is needed.
Fluence is the energy delivered per square centimetre. Too low is ineffective, too high risks burns.
Spot size and cooling change how deep the energy travels and how comfortable the treatment feels.

lessons.title: Laser Safety Protocols & Eye Protection
lessons.summary: A practical handout covering the safety controls every laser room needs before the first client walks in.
points: Always use wavelength-specific eyewear with the correct optical density for both the client and the operator.
Control the treatment room with warning signage, closed doors and no reflective jewellery or surfaces.
Perform a patch test and wait 24 to 48 hours before a full treatment on new clients.
Keep a treatment log of settings, skin response and any adverse events for every session.

questions.q: Which principle explains how a laser damages the hair follicle while sparing the surrounding skin?
What does 'fluence' describe in laser treatments?
options: The colour of the laser beam
The number of pulses per session
The cooling temperature of the handpiece

questions.q: Why must both the client and the operator wear wavelength-specific eyewear?
options: It is only required for tattoo removal
Laser light can cause permanent retinal injury

lessons.title: Fitzpatrick Skin Typing for Indian Skin
lessons.summary: Most Indian clients fall between Fitzpatrick types three and five, which changes how aggressively you can treat.
points: The Fitzpatrick scale classifies skin from type I, which always burns, to type VI, which never burns.
Higher skin types have more epidermal melanin that competes with the follicle for laser energy.
Longer wavelengths such as 1064 nm Nd:YAG are safer for darker skin because they bypass epidermal melanin.
Recent tanning temporarily raises the effective skin type and calls for lower settings or postponement.

lessons.title: Consultation, Consent & Contraindications
lessons.summary: Use this checklist to run a structured consultation and identify clients who should not be treated.
points: Record medical history, medications such as isotretinoin or photosensitisers, and any history of keloids.
Defer treatment during pregnancy, active skin infection or immediately after sun exposure.
Explain expected results, number of sessions and possible side effects before taking written consent.
Screen for hormonal conditions such as PCOS that may need more sessions and medical co-management.

questions.q: Most Indian clients fall within which Fitzpatrick skin type range?
options: Fitzpatrick typing does not apply to Indian skin

questions.q: Which wavelength is generally the safest choice for darker skin types?
Which of these should defer a laser hair reduction session?
options: Isotretinoin use in the last six months
Shaving the area the day before

lessons.title: Choosing Parameters: Diode, Nd:YAG & Alexandrite
lessons.summary: Selecting the right device and parameters is the difference between great results and avoidable complications.
points: Diode lasers around 810 nm balance melanin absorption and depth, making them versatile for types II to IV.
Alexandrite at 755 nm is highly effective on fair skin with dark hair but riskier on darker skin.
Start conservatively, look for the endpoint of perifollicular redness and swelling, then adjust.
Space sessions four to eight weeks apart to target hairs in the active anagen growth phase.

lessons.title: Aftercare & Managing Side Effects
lessons.summary: Aftercare instructions and a quick-reference guide to recognising and handling side effects.
points: Advise broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every day and avoid sun exposure for at least two weeks.
Mild redness and swelling are expected and settle within 24 to 48 hours with cool compresses.
Blistering, crusting or pigment change are warning signs that need review and parameter correction.
Avoid waxing or threading between sessions because the laser needs the hair root intact.

questions.q: What is the desired clinical endpoint immediately after a laser hair reduction pulse?
Why are sessions spaced four to eight weeks apart?
options: To let the device cool down
To target hairs in the anagen growth phase
Because lasers lose power between sessions

questions.q: Which hair removal method should clients avoid between laser sessions?

courses.title: Advanced Skin Rejuvenation & Anti-Ageing
courses.short: Design evidence-based anti-ageing treatment plans combining topicals, in-clinic procedures and lifestyle guidance.
courses.long: Built for practising aestheticians and skin therapists who want to move beyond basic facials. You will understand the biology of ageing skin, compare active ingredients such as retinoids, vitamin C and peptides, evaluate in-clinic options like microneedling and radiofrequency, and learn to build structured 12-week rejuvenation plans with realistic expectations and measurable outcomes.
outcomes: Differentiate intrinsic and extrinsic ageing and explain their visible signs
Choose between retinoids, vitamin C and peptides for different clients
Recommend microneedling or radiofrequency with clear indications
Build and review a 12-week rejuvenation plan with standardised photos
Set honest expectations that turn first-time clients into long-term clients

certification.title: Advanced Skin Rejuvenation Certificate
certification.description: Awarded after completing all modules and passing each assessment.

outcomeHighlights.title: Premium Services
outcomeHighlights.description: Offer higher-value anti-ageing programmes instead of one-off facials.

outcomeHighlights.title: Evidence-Based
outcomeHighlights.description: Every recommendation is grounded in published dermatology research.

lessons.title: Intrinsic vs Extrinsic Ageing
lessons.summary: Skin ages through two overlapping processes: the genetic clock we cannot stop, and environmental damage we can control.
points: Intrinsic ageing is driven by genetics and time, gradually thinning the skin and slowing cell turnover.
Extrinsic ageing comes from UV exposure, pollution, smoking and poor sleep, and causes most visible ageing.
Photoageing shows up as coarse wrinkles, uneven pigmentation and loss of elasticity.
Daily sun protection is the single most effective anti-ageing intervention available.

lessons.title: Collagen, Elastin & the Extracellular Matrix
lessons.summary: A reference sheet on the structural proteins that keep skin firm, and how they change with age.
points: Collagen provides tensile strength. Production falls roughly one percent per year from the mid-twenties.
Elastin allows skin to recoil. UV exposure fragments elastin fibres, which causes sagging.
Hyaluronic acid binds water in the dermis, keeping skin plump and hydrated.
Fibroblasts produce these proteins and can be stimulated by retinoids, peptides and controlled injury.

questions.q: Which factor is responsible for most visible signs of skin ageing?
options: UV exposure and other environmental factors

questions.q: Which structural protein gives skin its tensile strength?
Which cells in the dermis produce collagen and elastin?

lessons.title: Retinoids, Vitamin C & Peptides
lessons.summary: Three ingredient families have the strongest evidence for improving the signs of ageing.
points: Retinoids increase cell turnover and stimulate collagen, but must be introduced slowly to limit irritation.
Vitamin C is an antioxidant that brightens skin and supports collagen. It works best in the morning under sunscreen.
Peptides act as signalling molecules that encourage repair with minimal irritation.
Combine actives gradually and check tolerance before adding the next product.

lessons.title: Microneedling and Radiofrequency Overview
lessons.summary: Compare two popular collagen-stimulating procedures and when to recommend each.
points: Microneedling creates controlled micro-injuries that trigger the skin's wound-healing response.
Radiofrequency heats the dermis to tighten existing collagen and stimulate new production.
Both typically need a course of three to six sessions spaced about four weeks apart.
Avoid treating active acne, infections, or clients who recently took isotretinoin.

questions.q: When is a vitamin C serum best applied?
Why should retinoids be introduced gradually?
options: To limit irritation while the skin adapts
They only work after six months

questions.q: How does microneedling stimulate collagen?
options: By creating controlled micro-injuries that trigger wound healing

lessons.title: Designing a 12-Week Rejuvenation Plan
lessons.summary: A structured plan turns individual treatments into measurable, lasting results.
points: Start with a baseline assessment and standardised photos under consistent lighting.
Weeks one to four build the home-care foundation: cleanser, antioxidant, retinoid and sunscreen.
Weeks five to twelve layer in-clinic procedures once the skin barrier is strong.
Review progress every four weeks and adjust based on photos and client feedback.

lessons.title: Client Communication & Expectation Setting
lessons.summary: Scripts and tips for honest conversations that build trust and long-term clients.
points: Explain that collagen remodelling takes three to six months to become visible.
Use before-and-after photos to show realistic, not exaggerated, outcomes.
Document the agreed plan, costs and aftercare in writing.
Schedule maintenance sessions to protect results over time.

questions.q: What should happen before starting any rejuvenation plan?
options: A baseline assessment with standardised photos

questions.q: Why is home care established before in-clinic procedures?
options: To strengthen the skin barrier first
In-clinic procedures don't need home care

questions.q: How long does visible collagen remodelling typically take?

courses.title: Chemical Peels Masterclass
courses.short: Master superficial and medium-depth chemical peels safely, with a special focus on darker skin tones.
courses.long: Chemical peels are among the most requested and most profitable treatments in any skin clinic, but they carry real risk when done poorly. This masterclass explains peel chemistry, depth classification and patient selection, then walks you step by step through priming, application, neutralisation and aftercare. You will finish with a complication-management toolkit designed for Indian skin.
outcomes: Compare AHAs, BHAs and TCA and choose the right agent for each client
Classify peels by depth and predict downtime
Prime skin correctly to reduce pigmentation risk
Perform a superficial peel using a step-by-step protocol
Recognise and manage peel complications early

certification.title: Chemical Peels Practitioner Certificate
certification.description: Complete the masterclass and pass every assessment to receive your certificate.

outcomeHighlights.title: Profitable Service
outcomeHighlights.description: Add one of the most requested treatments to your service menu.

outcomeHighlights.title: Fewer Complications
outcomeHighlights.description: Learn the priming and aftercare steps that prevent most problems.

lessons.title: AHAs, BHAs & TCA Explained
lessons.summary: Each peeling agent behaves differently on the skin, and choosing the right one starts with understanding its chemistry.
points: Alpha hydroxy acids such as glycolic and lactic acid are water-soluble and loosen surface skin cells.
Beta hydroxy acids such as salicylic acid are oil-soluble, so they penetrate pores and suit acne-prone skin.
Trichloroacetic acid, or TCA, causes protein coagulation, and its depth depends on concentration.
Lower pH and higher concentration both increase a peel's strength and its risk.

lessons.title: Peel Depth Classification
lessons.summary: A quick reference for classifying peels by depth, typical agents and downtime.
points: Very superficial peels affect only the stratum corneum, with little or no downtime.
Superficial peels reach the full epidermis and cause light flaking for a few days.
Medium-depth peels reach the papillary dermis and need about a week of recovery.
Deep peels such as phenol reach the reticular dermis and are rarely suitable for darker skin.

questions.q: Which peeling agent is oil-soluble and well suited to acne-prone skin?
How does trichloroacetic acid (TCA) work on the skin?
Which peel depth reaches the papillary dermis?

lessons.title: Skin Priming & Pre-Peel Preparation
lessons.summary: Good results start two to four weeks before the peel, with careful priming.
points: Priming with a retinoid or mild acid evens out penetration on the day of the peel.
Tyrosinase inhibitors such as azelaic acid reduce the risk of post-peel pigmentation in darker skin.
Stop retinoids three to five days before the procedure to avoid over-penetration.
Strict sun protection during the priming phase is essential.

lessons.title: Step-by-Step Superficial Peel Protocol
lessons.summary: A printable protocol for performing a superficial glycolic acid peel in the clinic.
points: Cleanse and degrease the skin, then protect sensitive areas around the eyes, nostrils and lips.
Apply the peel evenly and time it precisely, watching for redness or frosting.
Neutralise glycolic acid peels with a buffering solution and rinse with cool water.
Finish with a bland moisturiser and broad-spectrum sunscreen before the client leaves.

questions.q: Why is skin primed before a chemical peel?
options: To even out penetration and reduce pigmentation risk

questions.q: When should retinoids typically be stopped before a peel?
options: They never need to be stopped

questions.q: How is a glycolic acid peel ended?
options: It is neutralised with a buffering solution and rinsed
It is wiped off with alcohol

lessons.title: Post-Inflammatory Hyperpigmentation Risk
lessons.summary: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, or PIH, is the most common peel complication in Indian skin.
points: PIH happens when inflammation triggers melanocytes to overproduce pigment.
Darker skin types, aggressive peels and sun exposure all increase the risk.
Choose gentler agents like mandelic or lactic acid, and build strength gradually.
Treat early PIH with sun protection, tyrosinase inhibitors and patience.

lessons.title: Complication Management Checklist
lessons.summary: What to do when a peel does not go to plan.
points: Excessive stinging or early frosting: neutralise or remove the peel immediately.
Prolonged redness: apply a calming barrier cream and review after 48 hours.
Infection or blistering: refer the client to a dermatologist promptly.
Document every complication and adjust the protocol for future sessions.

questions.q: What is the most common chemical peel complication in darker skin types?
Which agents are gentler choices for clients at high risk of PIH?
What should you do if a client shows blistering or signs of infection after a peel?

courses.title: Acne & Pigmentation Management
courses.short: Assess, grade and treat acne and pigmentation with combination protocols that deliver visible results.
courses.long: Acne and pigmentation are the two concerns that bring the most clients into Indian skin clinics. This course teaches you what drives them, how to grade severity consistently, and how to design combination treatment pathways using topicals, peels, lasers and home care, while knowing exactly when to refer to a dermatologist.
outcomes: Explain the four factors behind acne formation
Grade acne severity consistently and know when to refer
Differentiate melasma, PIH and sun damage
Use a Wood's lamp to judge pigment depth
Build combination treatment and home-care plans

certification.title: Acne & Pigmentation Specialist Certificate
certification.description: Earned after completing every module and assessment in the course.

outcomeHighlights.title: Most-Requested Concerns
outcomeHighlights.description: Confidently handle the concerns clients ask about most.

outcomeHighlights.title: Better Retention
outcomeHighlights.description: Structured plans keep clients coming back for follow-ups.

lessons.title: Pathophysiology of Acne
lessons.summary: Acne develops when four factors combine inside the pilosebaceous unit.
points: Excess sebum production, often driven by androgens, creates an oily environment.
Abnormal shedding of skin cells blocks the follicle and forms a comedone.
Cutibacterium acnes bacteria multiply inside the blocked follicle.
Inflammation turns comedones into red papules, pustules, nodules and cysts.

lessons.title: Grading Acne Severity
lessons.summary: A grading worksheet to record acne severity consistently at every visit.
points: Grade one: comedones only, meaning open blackheads and closed whiteheads.
Grade two: comedones with a few inflamed papules and pustules.
Grade three: many papules and pustules with occasional nodules.
Grade four: nodules and cysts with a risk of scarring, which requires dermatologist referral.

questions.q: What forms when abnormal shedding of skin cells blocks a follicle?
Which bacteria are associated with acne?
Which acne grade requires referral to a dermatologist?
options: Grade four, with nodules and cysts

lessons.title: Melasma, PIH & Sun Damage
lessons.summary: Not all dark patches are the same, and the right treatment depends on the cause.
points: Melasma appears as symmetrical brown patches on the cheeks and forehead, linked to hormones and UV.
Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation follows acne, injury or aggressive treatments.
Solar lentigines are well-defined sun spots caused by cumulative UV exposure.
Visible light and heat can worsen melasma, so tinted sunscreens are especially helpful.

lessons.title: Wood's Lamp & Pigment Assessment
lessons.summary: How to use a Wood's lamp and a structured assessment to judge pigment depth.
points: Epidermal pigment looks more pronounced under a Wood's lamp, while dermal pigment does not.
Epidermal pigment responds faster to topicals and peels than dermal pigment.
Photograph pigment under consistent lighting to track progress.
Record triggers such as pregnancy, contraceptives and sun exposure.

questions.q: Which pigmentation pattern is typically symmetrical on the cheeks and forehead?
Under a Wood's lamp, which type of pigment appears more pronounced?
Why are tinted sunscreens especially helpful for melasma?
options: They also block visible light that can worsen melasma

lessons.title: Combining Topicals, Peels & Lasers
lessons.summary: Combination treatment gets better results than any single approach.
points: Start with topicals such as retinoids, azelaic acid or niacinamide to build a foundation.
Add salicylic or mandelic peels every two to four weeks for active acne and mild pigmentation.
Consider low-fluence Q-switched Nd:YAG for stubborn pigment, with great caution in melasma.
Always pair procedures with strict sun protection to prevent relapse.

lessons.title: Home-Care Regimens that Work
lessons.summary: Simple morning and evening routines you can hand to clients.
points: Morning: gentle cleanser, antioxidant serum, oil-free moisturiser and SPF 50.
Evening: gentle cleanser, a targeted active such as adapalene or azelaic acid, and moisturiser.
Introduce one new product at a time and patch test it first.
Avoid picking, harsh scrubs and unverified home remedies.

questions.q: How often are superficial salicylic or mandelic peels typically repeated for active acne?
Which measure is essential alongside every pigmentation procedure?
What is the best way to introduce new home-care products?
options: One at a time with a patch test

courses.title: Foundations of Skin Science
courses.short: A free starter course on skin anatomy, skin types and common concerns, the perfect first step into aesthetics.
courses.long: New to the beauty and aesthetics industry? Start here. This free course explains how skin is built, what it does, how to identify skin types and the most common concerns you will see in clients. It is also a great way to experience the Quantum Education learning platform before enrolling in a professional programme.
outcomes: Name the three layers of the skin and what each one does
List the key functions of skin
Identify normal, oily, dry, combination and sensitive skin
Recognise the most common skin concerns in Indian clients

certification.title: Skin Science Foundations Badge
certification.description: Complete both modules to unlock your foundations badge.

outcomeHighlights.title: Try the Platform
outcomeHighlights.description: Experience lessons, PDFs and quizzes before buying a course.

outcomeHighlights.title: Build Your Base
outcomeHighlights.description: Every professional course builds on these fundamentals.

lessons.title: The Layers of the Skin
lessons.summary: Skin is the body's largest organ, made of three main layers with very different jobs.
points: The epidermis is the outer protective layer and contains melanocytes that produce pigment.
The dermis contains collagen, elastin, blood vessels, hair follicles and sweat glands.
The hypodermis, or subcutaneous layer, stores fat and cushions the body.
The epidermis renews itself roughly every 28 days in young adults, and more slowly with age.

lessons.title: Skin Functions Cheat Sheet
lessons.summary: A one-page summary of everything skin does for the body.
points: Protection against microbes, chemicals and UV radiation.
Temperature regulation through sweating and blood flow.
Sensation of touch, pressure, pain and temperature.
Vitamin D synthesis when exposed to sunlight.

questions.q: Which skin layer contains melanocytes?
Which layer contains collagen, blood vessels and hair follicles?
Roughly how often does the epidermis renew in young adults?

lessons.title: Identifying Skin Types
lessons.summary: Recognising skin type is the foundation of every recommendation you make.
points: Normal skin is balanced, with small pores and few concerns.
Oily skin shows shine and enlarged pores, especially across the T-zone.
Dry skin feels tight and may flake because it produces less oil.
Combination skin is oily in the T-zone and normal or dry on the cheeks, while sensitive skin reacts easily.

lessons.title: Common Skin Concerns in India
lessons.summary: An overview of the concerns you will see most often in Indian clients.
points: Pigmentation and uneven skin tone, including melasma and tanning.
Acne and acne marks, often worsened by heat and humidity.
Dullness and dehydration caused by pollution and sun exposure.
Unwanted hair, which drives strong demand for laser hair reduction.

questions.q: Which skin type shows shine and enlarged pores across the T-zone?
How is combination skin usually described?
options: Oily T-zone with normal or dry cheeks

questions.q: Which concern drives strong demand for laser hair reduction in India?

courses.title: Laser Safety Officer Essentials
courses.short: Learn to run a safe laser clinic: hazard classes, protective controls and daily safety audits.
courses.long: Every clinic that operates medical lasers needs someone who understands laser safety. This short course covers laser classifications, nominal hazard zones, protective eyewear and the standard operating procedures that keep clients and staff safe. It is ideal for clinic managers, therapists and anyone preparing to take on laser safety responsibilities.
outcomes: Explain laser classes and why aesthetic lasers are Class 4
Map the nominal hazard zone in a treatment room
Write a practical laser safety SOP
Run a daily safety audit before treatments begin

certification.title: Laser Safety Essentials Certificate
certification.description: Pass both assessments to receive your laser safety certificate.

outcomeHighlights.title: Compliance Ready
outcomeHighlights.description: Put safety documentation in place before audits and inspections.

outcomeHighlights.title: Safer Teams
outcomeHighlights.description: Give every staff member a clear, repeatable safety routine.

lessons.title: Laser Classes & Hazard Zones
lessons.summary: Lasers are grouped into classes according to their potential to cause harm.
points: Class 1 lasers are safe under normal use, while Class 4 lasers can injure eyes and skin and ignite materials.
Almost all aesthetic lasers are Class 4 and need strict controls.
The nominal hazard zone is the area where exposure can exceed safe limits.
Reflections from mirrors, jewellery and metal instruments can extend the hazard.

lessons.title: Nominal Hazard Zone Worksheet
lessons.summary: A worksheet to map hazard zones and controls in your treatment room.
points: Mark the treatment chair, laser position and doors on a simple room plan.
Identify reflective surfaces and cover or remove them.
List the required eyewear by wavelength and optical density.
Display warning signs at every entry point while the laser is in use.

questions.q: Which laser class do most aesthetic lasers belong to?
What is the nominal hazard zone?
options: The area where exposure can exceed safe limits

questions.q: Why should reflective jewellery be removed in the laser room?
options: Reflections can extend the hazard to eyes and skin

lessons.title: Building a Laser Safety SOP
lessons.summary: A written standard operating procedure makes safety repeatable for every staff member.
points: Define who is authorised to operate each device and how they are trained.
Include pre-treatment checks for eyewear, signage, device self-test and fire safety.
Describe exactly what to do in an incident, from eye exposure to burns.
Review and sign off the SOP at least once a year.

lessons.title: Daily Safety Audit Checklist
lessons.summary: A printable checklist to complete before the first treatment of the day.
points: Eyewear for every wavelength is present, clean and undamaged.
Warning signs and door interlocks are working.
Device calibration and self-test are completed and logged.
The fire extinguisher and first-aid kit are accessible.

questions.q: What should a laser safety SOP define?
options: Who is authorised to operate each device

questions.q: How often should a laser safety SOP be reviewed at minimum?
Which item belongs on a daily safety audit checklist?
options: Checking eyewear is present and undamaged

courses.short: Coming soon: a hands-on guide to microneedling for scars, texture and fine lines.
courses.long: This course is still being produced. It will cover device selection, needle depth, combining microneedling with serums and growth factors, and safe protocols for acne scarring on darker skin types.
outcomes: Choose between pen, roller and RF microneedling devices
Select needle depth by indication and facial zone

outcomeHighlights.title: Scar Revision
outcomeHighlights.description: Treat one of the most requested concerns after acne.

lessons.title: How Microneedling Works
lessons.summary: Microneedling uses fine needles to create controlled channels in the skin that kick-start collagen production.
points: Each micro-channel triggers inflammation, proliferation and remodelling phases of healing.
Needle depth is chosen by indication, from 0.25 mm for texture to 1.5 mm or more for scars.
Topical serums penetrate far better through freshly created channels.
Results build over a course of sessions spaced about four weeks apart.

lessons.title: Device Selection & Needle Depth Guide
lessons.summary: A comparison of microneedling devices and a needle depth reference by facial zone.
points: Dermarollers are inexpensive but give less control over depth and angle.
Automated pens allow precise depth adjustment and faster, more even treatment.
RF microneedling adds heat for extra tightening and scar remodelling.
Use shallower depths on the forehead and around the eyes, and deeper settings on cheeks for scars.
